newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus nationalists protest against Russia union.
newsitem.headline: Belarus nationalists protest against Russia union.

text.p: About 4,000 people marched through the capital of Belarus on Wednesday chanting "Independence!", in protest at an outline Union Treaty signed by the Russian and Belarussian presidents in Moscow earlier in the day.

Witnesses said the march through Minsk was mostly peaceful but police detained at least 10 people angered by the treaty, which they believe would return Belarus to domination by Moscow after five years of independence from the Soviet Union.
Police allowed the march to go ahead, but plucked a few protesters out of the crowd and detained them. There were minor scuffles but no major clashes, the witnesses said.

A few hundred communist supporters of President Alexander Lukashenko's policy of union with Russia gathered separately in a park in central Minsk. They did not clash with the protesters marching through the city centre.
Lukashenko signed the outline Union Treaty with Russian President Boris Yeltsin, who said it does not create a single state and that each side maintains its sovereignty.

It was a far cry from a document which Lukashenko had backed but was opposed by Russian liberals. That version would have put him closer to his dream of eventually uniting his former Soviet republic of 10 million people with the vast Russian Federation.
